I checked the domestic research against re-fetched sources and redid the NAIP measurements. Two cited facts are wrong, one roof section was misread, and every NAIP height should come down about 5 %. The Verification section is appended to the research note and the corrections are in the spec. I changed nothing in js/ or data/ and committed nothing. (spec_itb.json and itb_verify.* in the working tree come from another agent, not from me.)

**Refuted**
- **"T1 skylight trusses 70 ft above the floor, four 180 × 30 ft reflectors"**: the SFO Museum page puts this artwork in the Dianne Feinstein International Terminal main hall (Level 3, dated 2000). "Harvey Milk Terminal 1" only appears in the page's menu of terminals. T1 Center therefore has no published height at all. The skylight-count "conflict" goes away: Airport Improvement 2020 says three skylights, which matches the three openings seen on NAIP. These figures belong to the ITB research.
- **BA-D DOF points "at the head corners" (24–25 ft)**: all three lie 24–37 m outside the BA-D outline, and the DOF horizontal accuracy is ±6 m, so they are not on the pier and cannot check its height. DOF 06-035332 (16 ft) is also on the apron, 9 m past the BA-F tip, not part of BA-F.
- **The research's own tower note** (axis 7 m east of the tower research) is not a real conflict. It came from the 2020 shadow scale below; with the corrected scale the axis lands at about −737 to −741.

**Corrected**
- **2020 shadow scale (sets every NAIP height)**: the research used 1.19 m of shadow per metre "± 0.03". At its own tower-shadow direction (87.4°) the sun path gives 1.226. I re-measured the direction at 88.1–88.9°, which gives 1.26–1.31. The BA-F DOF control fits about 1.27 best; only the BA-A lean check supports 1.19. I adopted 1.25 (range 1.19–1.31), so the heights below are about 5 % lower than in the research:

| Roof | Research | Adopted | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| BA-A (control) | 18.74 m | 17.83 m | 16.94–18.74 m (ITB research: 17.0) |
| BA-E fascia | 13.51 m | 12.85 m | 12.21–13.51 m |
| BA-F north-east arm | 11.03 m | 10.49 m | 9.97–11.03 m (DOF: 10.36 m) |
| BA-D head (low confidence) | 8.92 m | 8.49 m | 8.07–8.93 m |
| BA-C (low confidence) | 7.54 m | 7.20 m | 6.99–7.53 m |

- **Boarding Area B is stepped, not one level**: measured on the south half only, the central PV field moves 3.40 m between 2020 and 2024, but the side bands and outer edges move only 2.25–2.30 m, so they are lower. The 2020 "dark perimeter strip" is the shadow of the raised central roof on the lower band; it is white roof in 2024. The research had combined the central roof's parallax with the outer edge's shadow bands.
  - Outer edges: 13.1 m (12.5–13.8). The research's 12.87 m was close only because two errors cancelled.
  - New raised central roof: 19.0 m (18.1–20.0). The roughly 6 m step is the clerestory Arup describes.
  - Recomputed edge overhang: about 2.3 m on the airfield side (was 3.3 m).
- **Smaller fixes**: PV row width 5.7–7.1 m (the 9.1–9.3 m pitch is confirmed). The T3W "22'-0"" is the sum of printed 10'+10'+2' dimensions, not a printed value. The author of photos p17–p20 is Benoît Prieur (the spec had HTML junk).

**Confirmed**
- **T3 levels** from the re-fetched design-review PDF: L1 11'-0", L2 27'-0", mezzanine 42'-6", L3 45'-0", roof high points R2 58'-6" and R3 81'-0", T3W parapet 66'-0".
- **Wall sections**: field 56'-00" with a 42" parapet, gatehouse 59'-07".
- **SFO Museum outlines**: confirmed as level-2 floor outlines.
- **The BA-E roof** is one level; its parallax is uniform at about 2.6 m.
- **Dates, areas, gate counts, PV and glazing figures** were all re-read in the original sources.
- **All 26 photo licences** match Commons.
- **The two-epoch method's algebra** holds, as long as every measurement belongs to the same roof edge.

**Still unknown**
- **T1 Center and T2 hall heights.** Nothing is published.
- **The datum of the T3 elevations.**
- **The exact 2020 sun.** The acquisition time of the 2020 image strips would pin every NAIP height to about ±2 %. I tried to read pole shadows of known height on NAIP 2020 instead, but none could be picked out at 0.6 m resolution.
- **BA-B north half and roof wells.** The parallax scan was not done there.
- **Truss rhythm and facade bays.** No source gives them.

The checks re-run with `python3 tools/buildings/dom_verify.py`, and `--apply` rewrites the spec records. NAIP 2020 and 2022 can still be fetched from Planetary Computer with `dom_naip_epochs.py`, so the missing second epoch is not a blocker.

BA-B section: an SFO/HKS section drawing or a scaled photo of the clerestory step; parallax scan of the north half and roof wells
T3 CDR elevation datum vs NAVD88 / apron (SFO Design & Construction)

result.summary:
I fact-checked the ITB research and appended a '## Verification' section to docs/research/buildings_itb.md. It holds 34 claims, each with a verdict and its evidence, plus sections V.2–V.4. Two values in tools/buildings/spec_itb.json were wrong and are corrected, with the old values kept. One measured width was refuted (Boarding Area G's ~33.5 m) and two numbers were relabelled. The 860 ft roof-length conflict is still open. Nothing was committed, and js/ and data/ are untouched.

How it was checked: tools/buildings/itb_verify.py repeats everything offline in about 5 s and writes tools/buildings/itb_verify.json (numbers only). Run with --apply, it writes the verdicts into the spec; all 65 items now carry a verification record. Because build_spec_itb.py regenerates the spec without them, run itb_verify.py --apply again after it.
- Re-fetched: the FAA DOF (file dated 2026-11-02), 15 source pages and the Commons licence records of all 24 photos. Each download's URL and licence is recorded in a SOURCES.json beside it.
- itb_naip_measure.py on the restored NAIP 2024 raster gives byte-identical output.
- The SEAONC page, previously read only as search snippets, now opens and was read in full.

**Verified**
- **DOF roof tops:** 06-035315 and 06-035316 are unchanged at 131 / 132 ft AGL, accuracy 1A. They were added to the DOF on 16 Oct 2013, so the survey predates NAIP 2024 and the re-roofing.
- **Column lines:** the two DOF points sit at u = +57.2 / −58.4 m from the relief-corrected centre. They are 115.5 m (379 ft) apart along the axis, which matches the 380 ft centre span. They mark the roof over the inner column lines (±190 ft), which independently supports the inferred column rhythm. The note's "+54.7 / −60.9 m" was measured from the uncorrected (as-imaged) centre; that is now corrected.
- **Now read first-hand (SEAONC):** five double-cantilever truss sets; 20 cantilevered columns rising from the level-3 departures floor; trusses up to 29 ft deep; 380 ft centre span; 160 ft end cantilevers; 860 ft overall; great hall 705 × 210 × up to 83 ft (so 83 ft is the interior height, not the roof height); Herrick, Mare Island, about 35 pieces by barge.
- **Axis:** 162.81°, from an independent fit to the west facade base (sd 0.15 m). That is the airport grid t-axis + 135°, and both piers also sit on the grid axes.
- **Width:** 65.4 m. The east eave rises and falls along the roof together with the west eave, so the measured "wing" profile is a height signal, not a curved plan.
- **Truss spacing:** 12.16 m = 39.9 ft, by autocorrelation over 207 rows (published 40 ft).
- **Sun:** solar-position formulas give 13:14 PDT and 72.39° elevation for the NAIP flight date.
- **Glazed tip bands:** confirmed visually.
- **Published figures:** levels, dates (10 Dec 2000 opening, 16 Jan 2024 renaming, 27 Jun 2024 ceremony, mid-2026 completion), 1.8 M sq ft, 267 isolators, the Boarding Area G facts (Tutor Perini) and 1,400 kW of PV were each found verbatim in the cached pages.
- **Photos:** all 24 licences and authors match the spec.

**Corrected**
- **Roof corners:** the stated outline is 255.06 m long, which contradicts the spec's own length of 252.68 m. It is replaced by corners from a frame-camera relief model fitted to the same five pole picks (252.87 × 65.39 m). The old corners are kept as an alternative.
- **Boarding Area A roof:** 17.0 → 17.9 m (range 16.9–18.8). The west band re-measures 8.79 m. The note subtracted a roof overhang, but an overhang moves both band edges equally and cancels out; its second method depended on the SFO Museum footprint.
- **Refuted:** Boarding Area G's measured roof width is 38.4 m between its parapets, not ~33.5 m. That matches the SFO Museum body width.
- **Weaker than stated:** the A pod rim band includes the pod's own shadow, so the pod rises 4.9–5.2 m above the main roof, not 7.5 m. That gives a pod top of 22.3–25.2 m against the DOF's 25.9 m.
- **Minor:** the 48.4 m lens skylight length is the as-imaged length; true is about 47.9 m.
- **Conflict:** gates at opening are 26 per SEAONC and 24 per Tutor Perini.

**New uncertainty and findings**
- **Relief model:** fitting the five pole shifts in both directions with a frame camera works better than the east-only model (rms 0.21 vs 0.54 m), and the shift direction turns with north–south position. But two of the five picks are by eye, and Boarding Area G's visible shadow contradicts a single frame there. The NAIP 2024 sensor is undocumented in any open source I found.
  - Roof length is therefore 252.6–255.1 m, still 7–9 m short of the published 860 ft (262.1 m).
  - With the inner columns fixed by the DOF pair, the visible cantilever beyond the outer column is about 145 ft, not 160 ft.
- **Centre section off-centre:** it sits 2.2 m north of the midpoint between the fascias. The south tip has a 3.6 m white strip beyond its glass; the north tip has 1.6 m.

**Still unknown:** the roof length conflict; the 320 ft truss length and 180 ft centre section (the AISC article is still blocked); the crown and tip heights, which rest on a photo I could not re-measure because Wikimedia returned HTTP 429; the level-3 floor (only bracketed at 9.6–14.8 m); pier pod heights; the 2026 roof's PV layout; the $75 M cost; and whether the skylights are lens- or D-shaped in plan.
open_questions: Roof length: NAIP 252.6-255.1 m vs 860 ft (262.1 m) published. The DOF pair confirms the 380 ft centre span, so the gap is in the end cantilevers (about 145 ft visible vs 160 ft published). An SFO record roof plan, a tip survey or the NAIP 2024 frame metadata would settle it.

NAIP 2024 sensor and mosaic seamlines: the north-south relief component is unresolved. The poles favour a frame camera (nadir about (-2768, 444)), but Boarding Area G contradicts a single frame. This sets the length range and the pier heights.
AISC Modern Steel Construction Feb 2000 is still unreadable (curl 403, WebFetch 403, web.archive.org connection reset), so the 320 ft truss length and 180 ft centre section remain snippet-only.
The crown and tip heights rest on the DimiCalifornia photo, which could not be re-fetched (Wikimedia HTTP 429). Re-run itb_photo_skyline.py once the rate limit clears.
Pier heights: A main roof 17.4-18.3 m, pods 22.3-25.2 m by relief against the DOF's 25.9 m; G 16.9 m (east-only relief model). No published elevations.
The 'SFO Museum G outline is 3-6 m NNE of the NAIP roof' claim was not re-checked.
The RADP NOP (main-hall and A/G expansions) was not re-fetched this round.

I fact-checked the landside building research and appended a `## Verification` section to `docs/research/buildings_landside.md` (section 14, same layout as the tower's). Every one of the 130 values in `spec_landside.json` now carries a verdict:
- 84 confirmed, 18 of them with a qualifier;
- 2 plausible;
- 4 disputed, 6 corrected and 1 refuted;
- 1 still unknown;
- 28 not re-checked;
- 4 new.

Corrected values keep their old fields and the reason under `corrected`.

**How I checked**
- 43 sources re-fetched and re-read.
- FAA DOF checked against the newer DOF.CSV of 2026-11-03.
- SFO Museum building records re-read.
- NAIP 2024 re-measured with methods different from the original:
  - a 2-D roof-shift scan;
  - the helix-drum facade bands, using the ITB pole calibration inside its valid range;
  - north shadows on flat ground, against the solar position for 20 May 2024.

**Refuted or corrected**
- **RCC "NAIP 19.5 m agrees with 66 ft":** refuted. The original used the third-strongest roof-shift peak and a lean model that doesn't hold in the North Field. The DOF survey puts the roof outline at 54 ft (three points) and 59 ft (one), all on the west side, not the NE corner. It also lists a 34-ft obstacle the research missed. The published 66 ft is confirmed as text but can't be the parapet height.
- **Central garage built 1981, replacing an earlier 1963–1981 garage:** corrected. The RADP historic resources study says Building 195 was built in phases from 1963 to 1981. The 1963–65 first section was partly demolished and absorbed, and the garage was completed in 1980–81.
- **Superbay layout:**
  - The cantilever is "over 230 ft from the center", so the "2 × 70 m + spine" breakdown is wrong.
  - NAIP shows a roof 165 m long with a 32 m spine (not 25–30 m).
  - Each side is folded into 8 bays of 17.3 m. This conflicts with Deep3DS's "50 foot wide structural bays", which the research missed.
- **One NAIP moment at about 13:25 for every building:** corrected. The Superbay area was imaged in the morning, so the roof-car counts aren't one moment.
- **One lean factor across the landside area:** refuted outside its calibrated range. The lean factor is about 0.30–0.33 m per m of height at the CAC and Long-Term Parking (LTP) Garage 1. The model gives 0.14–0.19 there.
- **LTP Garage 2 "four seismically isolated structures":** corrected to "seismically separated". The count of four rests only on the Buehler page, which no longer loads.

**Disputed**
- **Garages A and G at 25–30 m:** NAIP puts the helix-drum tops at 39.6 m (A) and 37.6 m (G), about ±2 m. The parking roof deck itself is still unmeasured.
- **Build years:** the RADP appendix gives 1994 for LTP Garage 1 and 1998 for the RCC; the SFO Museum records give approximate years of 1997 and 2000.

**Confirmed**
- Central garage: 81 ft, five levels, 3.68 M sq ft, 6,460 spaces, 200-ft void (measured hole 58.7–59.0 m).
- Garages A and G: nine levels, AirTrain at Level 7.
- LTP Garage 2: 6 levels, 12-ft floors, 3,600 stalls, completed 2020.
- RCC: 5 levels, 1,488,000 sq ft, 2,485 stalls, Building 780.
- Grand Hyatt: 12 stories, 4th-floor lobby, Building 55, opened 7 Oct 2019.
- CAC: 4 stories at 15 ft, 135,000 sq ft (the 136,000 figure is gone), Phase II addendum. It is Building 674.
- CAC height of about 64 ft: within ±1.5 m. The north shadow gives 17.4–19.2 m; the old 28.6 m scan value is refuted.
- Superbay: four bays, six office levels, 120 ft inside, DOF 135 ft. That DOF entry is a 2011 change, not part of the 2013 survey batch.
- LTP Garage 1: the DOF points of 86 and 91 ft are confirmed. A new shadow measurement puts the north-end parapet at 15.9–16.8 m, so those points are elements about 10 m higher.
- AirTrain: car size 9'3" × 39'6", $430 M, 1,900-ft extension, the "50 ft" and "35–40 ft" quotes, opening 24 Feb / official 3 Mar 2003.
- All nine footprints, the 2018 parking supply, and the A/G station-name swap in the SFO Museum data.

**Still unknown**
- Grand Hyatt height (provisional 44 m). Its SFO Museum outline doesn't trace the main slab.
- Garage A/G and LTP Garage 2 roof decks.
- What the 81 ft and 66 ft actually measure.
- The 13 photo licences: the Commons API returned HTTP 429, so I couldn't re-check them.

**Tooling**
- `tools/buildings/landside_verify.py` runs offline in about 15 s. `tools/buildings/landside_verify_apply.py` writes the corrections into the spec.
- `build_spec_landside.py` now calls the apply step. I checked that a rebuild plus apply gives an identical spec and that re-running changes nothing.
- `landside_fetch.py` now falls back to `pdftotext` when PyMuPDF is missing.
- I added `SOURCES.json` files beside the cached downloads.

Nothing in `js/` or `data/` was touched, and nothing was committed.

What the published 81 ft (Central garage) and 66 ft (RCC) measure. The DOF puts the RCC roof outline at 54–59 ft.

Each sheet has a title block, scale bars, a north arrow on plans, dimension lines and level marks. Every value carries a [tag source] label, and the line style also shows the tag: pub black solid, obs blue solid, inf orange dashed italic, unknown grey dotted, app magenta.

BT-01 also shows the cab x bounds, the OE/AAA sites, the cab as imaged in four NAIP epochs, and the app's shaft and cab.
- **ITB** (BI-01 roof plans: key 1:2500, hall 1:750, BA-A / BA-G; BI-02 west and north elevations; BI-03 long and cross sections). The hall roof is relief-corrected: 252.9 × 65.4 m, 5 truss lines at 12.12 m, 5 lens skylights, glazed tip bands, the DOF tops at 40.08 m and the eave profile. Column lines and truss taper are marked inferred. The 860 ft published length is drawn next to the measured length as a conflict.
- **Domestic** (BD-01 plan 1:2500; BD-02 pier cross-sections 1:500 and the T3 West CDR wall sections and level datum 1:200). The plan shows the SFO Museum level-2 outlines, the measured lean-free roof edges, the pier heights with ranges, and the refuted DOF points.
- **Landside** (BL-01 key plan 1:5000; BL-02 roof plans 1:2000; BL-03 long-face elevations 1:1000). All buildings and DOF points, including the Superbay spine and roof bays and the United MOC from its imaged roof.
- **BX-01, app vs spec** (A2): a 28-row table, a heights dot plot, and tower and ITB profile overlays. The biggest gaps:
  - The ITB roof is built to the 83-ft interior height (21–26.5 m against 34.9–40.1 m) and sits 35 m east of the measured roof, turned 2.9°.
  - The tower shaft is 7.2 m south of the inferred axis; the cab roof is D 20.3 against 14.3–14.75, and the rim is 1–5.5 m too low.
  - Every pier is 14.6 m against measured 7.2–19.0 m.
  - The Superbay, RCC and Hyatt heights are off, and the MOC is not built.

**Deviations method.** NAIP roofs are displaced by relief, so a drawn roof edge is compared at its predicted imaged position (height × lean). Footprints are checked only on faces towards the camera nadir, where the facade base is visible. The lean model is per area: a frame model fitted to the FAA DOF poles for the ITB and tower, per-pier two-epoch leans for the domestic piers, the measured North Field lean, and a fitted (circular) lean at the Superbay. Each edge's offset is in deviations.json, and the README explains how to read the results.

**Results.**
- SFO Museum outlines match the visible facade bases within about 1 m (the Superbay is 2.8 m off).
- The domestic level-2 outlines are 1–3 m off the roofs, as the spec says.
- The ITB roof is consistent to 0.3 m, but that check uses the same imagery the roof was measured on.
- The frame model predicts the NAIP cab disc within (1.1, 1.1) m for a 67.36 m rim and (2.9, 1.0) m for 64.0 m. That leans towards a 221-ft rim but does not settle it, because the cab x is itself ±5 m.

**README.md** has the sheet list, what is verified / inferred / unknown for each group, the overlay method, a results table and the limits.

findings.where: BT-02 view B (WNW landside elevation); tools/buildings/draw_tower.py draw_blades(): wo = w1/2 + 5.5
findings.problem: The SW wing is drawn about 3 m inside the flare silhouette. The pale flare circle forms the right-hand (SSW) outline at the top, with the narrower wing inside it. In the photos the wing itself is the SW silhouette: a flat top and a rounded corner, reaching well beyond where the flare circle would be.
findings.evidence:
Drawing, full-resolution crop at 29.5 px/m: the cab centre is at x 1004. The left flare is at -10.4 m, the right flare outline at +13.6 m and the wing's outer edge at +10.5 m. Code: the wing's outer edge is at u = 3.4 + 5.5 = 8.9 m from the axis, against a flare radius of 12.0 m at +58.9.
Photos t3 (Famartin 2025-08-12, CC BY-SA 4.0, bearing 319) and t4 (same author, bearing 338), scaled by cab roof = 192 px = 15.2 m:
- The right-hand silhouette is the wing, at 184 px (t3) and 199 px (t4) from the cab centre, i.e. 14.5 m and 15.7 m. The left (NE) flare is at 131 px in both, i.e. 10.4 m. The ratio is 1.40-1.52.
- The wing extends 88 px (t3) and 83 px (t4) past the ribbon's right edge, i.e. 7.0 m and 6.6 m. The drawing uses 5.5 m.

findings.where: BT-02 view A (ESE airside elevation), upper slot band 48.1-56.1 (F1); draw_tower.py draw_tower_elev(): V.poly(..., hatch='////'). Also view B (ribbon=True branch draws no slots)

The hatch reads as a continuous louvred band at the wrong angle. View B leaves out the slots that are visible on the NE flank next to the ribbon.

findings.where: BT-02 view A: the single long inclined slot, 22.0-40.2 m (F1); draw_tower.py: V.poly([(0.6,a2),(1.6,a2),(3.4,b2),(2.4,b2)])
findings.problem: The long diagonal slot twists only about half as much as in the photos. In the elevation it looks almost vertical (5.6 degrees). From the airside it reads as a pronounced diagonal slash.
findings.evidence:
Drawing: the slot centre runs from u 1.1 to u 2.9 m while the radius grows from 5.05 to 6.6 m, i.e. from 0.22 R to 0.44 R. That is 13 degrees of azimuth, 5.6 degrees from vertical as drawn.
t1, traced by the darkest pixel in each row between h 24 and 40 m: the slot centre runs from +0.28 R to +0.70 R, i.e. about 28 degrees of azimuth and about 11.6 degrees from vertical. t2, taken from gate C11 and lower, gives about 40 degrees.
The azimuth sweep does not depend on the viewing direction. The shaft itself is right: the profile in t1 matches the drawn F1 diameters within 0.5 m at seven stations (59.6: 23.4 vs 23.6; 56.3: 21.7 vs 22.1; 48.6: 16.6 vs 17.1; 43.5: 14.0 vs 14.5; 38.7: 12.3 vs 12.7; 35.1: 11.2 vs 11.6; 27.7: 10.1 vs 10.3). findings.problem: The cab floats. Between the flare-top deck and the glass sill there is a blank band 0.85 m high (F1: 60.60 to 61.45; F2: 57.6 to 58.4). The level label '+60.6 cab floor (sill band)' names it, but nothing is drawn there. The real cab stands on a solid dark plinth.

findings.where: BI-02 view 1 (ITB west elevation), the glass wall; draw_itb.py (one uniform fill, with the note 'three layers of ceramic frit ...')

findings.evidence:
i1 (Kulikovsky 2007, CC BY 3.0), i4 (DimiCalifornia 2005, public domain), i2 (2014) and i3 (2017) all show it.
- Width of the clear bay: in i4, x 730-1320 around a centre of 1025 = +-295 px; with the left tip at 950 px = 126.45 m that is +-39 m. In i1, +-323/327 px of 971 = +-42 m.

- The bay is therefore about 80 m wide, much wider than the centre arch (notches at +-27 m).

findings.fix: Draw the clear central bay (about 80 m, obs photos) with the lettering band, and the fritted side bays with the clear strip under the canopy. Check the head height of the central glazing against i1 / i4.

findings.where: BD-01, Boarding Area B (north and middle of the pier); spec bab.roof_wells, bab.pv_layout, bab.clerestory
findings.problem: Only a 62 m patch of BA-B's raised roof is drawn, hatched at the south end (t -1238..-1176). The rest of the pier carries only the text 'not measured'. NAIP 2024 clearly images roof features along the whole Harvey Milk T1 pier: the central PV field, three long planted sunken roof wells on the WNW side crossed by two bridges, and two skylight grids. Seen from above, these are the most recognisable things about this pier.
findings.fix: Draw the central field, the three wells with their bridges, and the skylights along the full pier from NAIP, lean-corrected and tagged obs. Leave heights unk where they are not measured.

findings.where: BD-02 section 1, 'Boarding Area E (north part)'; spec bae.roof [pub]
findings.problem: BA-E is drawn as one flat rectangle (42.9 x 12.85 m), with 'tapered roof edge over clerestory glazing' as text only. The published design and the 2025 aerial show a stepped section: a raised central roof whose thin tapered edge overhangs a recessed glass clerestory / end wall, between lower roofs on both sides.
findings.evidence:
Spec bae.roof [pub]: 'With tapered edges overhanging clerestory glazing ...'.
a1 (Pi.1415926535, Sept 2025, CC BY-SA 4.0), crop of the pier head north of the tower with United aircraft (identified as BA-E by position and airline, not verified):
- a raised PV-covered central roof with a knife-thin edge projecting over a full-height recessed glass wall;
- lower flat roofs on both flanks, below the raised roof.
BA-B in the same sheet is drawn stepped; BA-E is not.
findings.fix: Draw BA-E stepped: the raised centre with the overhanging tapered edge, the clerestory band and the lower side roofs. Tag the step heights inf / unk until measured.

findings.where: Domestic set (BD-01 / BD-02): no landside elevations for T1 / T2 / T3; spec t1c.landside_facade [pub], t2.landside [pub]
findings.problem: The faces that most people see (from the departures roadways, the AirTrain and the central garage) are not drawn anywhere. The domestic set has only pier cross-sections and the T3W CDR airside wall sections.

findings.where: BL-03 view 4, Superbay hangar (Bldg 1060) section across the spine; spec sb_layout [obs, CORRECTED 2026-11-04]
findings.problem: The Superbay is drawn as a flat-topped 165 m slab at the 36.58 m interior height, with the 32 m spine box rising to 42.67 m. The spec's own layout calls for cantilevered folded roofs (8 bays of 17.3 m on each side) and doors on the WNW and ESE faces. A flat box loses the building's character: roofs cantilevering out from a central spine.
findings.fix: Draw the cantilever roof profile falling from the spine to the tips (tip height unk). Show the fold ridges in a long-face view and the door openings, tagged inf / unk.

findings.where: BL-03 view 2, Grand Hyatt at SFO (Bldg 55); spec gh_plan_shape, gh_facade [obs]
findings.problem: The Grand Hyatt is drawn as a plain 12-storey box with a uniform floor grid and a hatched 40-48 m top band. The massing features that are already in the spec are left out: the dark podium, the taller straight block at the north end, the dark stepped penthouse and the corner masts. The concave east face is not indicated either.

findings.where: BL-03 view 1 / 2, International Garages A and G; draw_landside.py (bands 25-41.5 / 25-40; drum top only as a marker at u 12)
findings.problem: Each whole 281-282 m face is drawn as a box with a shaded 25-41.5 m (A) or 25-40 m (G) band. The helix drum, which is what sets the top value, appears only as a point marker. The garage therefore reads as a slab up to 41.5 m tall, and its recognisable parts are missing: the cylindrical helix drum, the AirTrain portal and the stair towers.
findings.evidence:
spec garage_ag_facade [obs]: 'light architectural precast concrete panels in a square grid; parking levels screened by prefabricated perforated metal panels with horizontal slots; cylindrical helix drum at the west end with continuous horizontal bands and arched openings at the top; square stair/elevator towers rise above the parapet'.
l1 (Pi.1415926535, Oct 2020, CC BY-SA 4.0) shows the drum as a separate curved concrete cylinder with horizontal bands next to the precast-grid block and the perforated screens, and the AirTrain guideway entering the station inside the garage at level 7 [pub].
The 9-level deck (8 ft 2 in clearance) is probably well below the drum top.
findings.fix: Draw the drum as its own cylinder at the west end with its 38-41.5 m top. Show the deck as unk (dotted) at a height inferred from the level count. Add the AirTrain portal at L7 and the stair towers.

findings.where: BT-02 view B; draw_blades() draws the ribbon centred on u = 0, while BT-01 sheet_plan draws the channel at hdg_vec(310)
findings.problem: The plan and the elevation disagree. BT-01 puts the ribbon channel at heading 310, but the WNW elevation (view from 297.7) draws the ribbon on the shaft axis. At azimuth 310 it should project to the NE of the axis, and more of the SW wing would show.
findings.evidence:
With right = hdg_vec(207.7), a ribbon at azimuth 310 projects at -0.21 R: -2.5 m at the flare (R 12) and -1.1 m at the base (R 5.2).
The photos fit an azimuth of about 300-310. The ribbon centre appears 4 m (t3, bearing 319) and 5.5 m (t4, bearing 338) right of the cab centre. Azimuth 310 predicts +0.16 R / +0.47 R; azimuth 300 predicts +0.33 R / +0.62 R.
findings.fix: Draw the ribbon and the blades at their plan azimuth in view B, shifted about 1-2.5 m to the NE, tagged inf. Adjust the wing (see the SW-wing finding).

findings.where: BT-02 A / B: masts and cladding
findings.problem: Only 4 masts are drawn, at u -5.6, -2.0, 3.4 and 6.0. The roof carries 9-12 masts of different heights around the rim, plus a railing and equipment. The cladding seams are drawn horizontal only; the real panel joints run diagonally (helically), parallel to the slots. That is the tower's surface texture.
findings.evidence: t1 shows 9 masts along the rim. t3 (crop of the top) shows about 12, the tallest about 4.5 m, plus a dish and the roof railing. In t1 and t2 the panel joints are clearly inclined, in the same sense as the slots. The drawn mast height (3.5 m) agrees with t1 (3.7 m).
findings.fix: Draw masts around the rim (count from t3) and note or indicate the diagonal panel grid. Tag both obs photo.

findings.where: BI-02 / BI-03: column heads and the departures canopy
findings.problem: Each column is drawn ending in a 2-strut V ('strut form schematic'). In the photos each white column branches into a fan of 4-6 or more struts into the trusses, a signature of the ITB. The departures canopy is only a dashed line at +14.5. Its inclined white support struts, which are prominent along the curb, are not drawn.
findings.evidence:
In i3 (Elizabeth K. Joseph 2017, CC BY 2.0) the near columns end in clusters of radiating struts. i4 shows about 4 members per column in elevation (2 each side) fanning out from about the glass-head level.
Canopy struts: inclined white members from the canopy up to the glass, at about 12 m spacing (i4 x 210, 300, 390 ... = 90 px at 0.133 m/px).
findings.fix: Draw a fan of 4-6 struts per column head and the canopy struts. Both inf / obs photo, schematic.

findings.where: BI-02 / BI-03 roof line near the tips; draw_itb.py wing() / roof_line()
findings.problem: The eave sags 0.5 m just inboard of each tip and then rises. The photos show the eave rising steadily from the tip.

findings.problem: There is no elevation or section for the ITB boarding areas. Their roof pods and glazing bands are carried only as labels ('3 raised lens pods ... heights unknown').
findings.fix: Add a long-face elevation of BA-A / BA-G with the pods as inf / unk heights and the glazing band.

findings.where: No sheet (ITB BA-G / T3 area)
findings.problem: An unidentified box-shaped rooftop tower appears in a 2018 photo and is not on any sheet.
findings.evidence: d2 (wbaiv, 2018-09-08, CC BY 4.0; titled 'SFO AirTrain Terminal 3 intl faceNorthWest') shows, at the left edge, a box tower about 2 storeys above a terminal roof with a dark window band and antennas. docs/research/atc.md lists ramp control 'Ramp G (West)'. The pre-2016 T2 tower's demolition was reviewed in 2017-2018 (buildings_tower.md). It is unclear whether this is that tower or a ramp tower, and whether it still stands.

result.summary:
I fixed all 23 round-2 findings, regenerated all 13 sheets, the 4 NAIP overlays and deviations.json (`python3 tools/buildings/draw.py`, about 65 s), and nothing in js/ or data/ was touched or committed. One finding is only partly accepted (the SW wing) and two reviewer numbers did not reproduce exactly; both are explained below.

Before acting on the photo claims I checked them against the cached reference photos (refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness; licences in its SOURCES.json) and NAIP 2024. The discrete slots, the long slot's twist, the cab plinth, the ITB's clear central bay and lettering, the BA-E step, the BA-B roof features, the T1 landside face and the Hyatt face were all confirmed.

**Tower (BT-01, BT-02, BT-03; draw_tower.py, draw_measure.py)**
- **F2 x bounds:** now computed for its 64.0 m rim: x ≥ −741.8 hard, ≥ −737.5 likely.
- **F2 cab check:** added an F2 check with the cab at its own likely bound (x −737.5). It gives delta (1.42, 0.98), |1.72| m, against F1's |1.53| m. That is "about as good", not the reviewer's (1.0, 1.0): moving the cab 1.5 m shifts the prediction 1.53 m. Still inconclusive.
- **Ribbon:** the plan keeps bearing 310°, the middle of the 300–320° photo range. Elevation B now draws the ribbon, both blades and the slots shifted by their plan position, up to 2.3 m left of the axis.
- **Number fixes:** the cab-roof z spread now reads 322.4–325.3 (±1.45 m); the spec note was corrected too. Mast tips read 233 ft.
- **Cab offset:** now stated as 1.8 m (1.5 E, 1.0 N), 1.6 m in the view plane.
- **CTBUH:** added as a note on BT-02.
- **Upper slots:** now discrete. From photo t1: 13 positions 27.7° apart, each about 1.4 m wide, sweeping about 20° with the top towards the NNE. None are drawn in the landside sector (230–335°); 2 show on the NE flank in view B.
- **Long slot:** now a helix from bearing 137° at its foot to 93° at its head, about 44°. Photos t1 and t2 independently give this; the reviewer estimated 28–35°.
- **Cab plinth:** dark ring, D 10.8 m, from the flare deck to the glass sill, drawn in both elevations and the section.
- **SW wing (partly rejected):** the photos t3 and t4 are taken from bearings 319° and 338°, not from view B's 297.7°.
  - The one plan point that reproduces both photos is the wing tip at 254°, 14.0 m from the axis. That gives 14.5 / 15.7 m right of the cab centre, against 14.5 / 15.7 measured, and 7.6 / 5.8 m beyond the ribbon edge, against 7.0 / 6.6.
  - Seen from 297.7° that tip projects at u +9.7, inside the round flare (12.0).
  - I widened the wing to that tip (was 8.9). A dotted line marks u +13.6, the silhouette if the wing wrapped south to about 208°, which the photos do not rule out. The flare outline stays visible beyond the wing.

**ITB (BI-01, BI-02, BI-03; draw_itb.py, draw_data.py)**
- **West wall:** now drawn inferred (orange dashed) as the band v −28.3 to −23.3, drawn at its middle −25.8. The two edges are the canopy-edge and wall-above-canopy readings. The canopy is cited to SEAONC ("entrance canopy"); BI-03 also shows the sight line to the camera. The old −26.3 is kept dotted, labelled valid only for a canopy no deeper than 2 m.
- **Hall width conflict:** dimensioned on BI-02 and BI-03: 64.0 m published against at most 61.0 m available under the roof. All three resolutions are listed. The published width is drawn from the wall and ends 5.5 m beyond the east eave.
- **Hump:** 40.08 is now tagged inferred (a fit anchored on the DOF mean). The 0.23 / 0.45 m misfit at the DOF points is stated, and the DOF values 39.93 / 40.23 are shown at their stations, including in the BI-03 section.
- **Skylights:** the lens shape is now tagged inferred, with the D-shaped alternative dotted.
- **Columns:** now in the inferred style.
- **830 ft:** fixed (was 829).
- **BI-02 west elevation:** now has the clear central bay (about 80 m) on its mullion grid, the "SAN FRANCISCO INTERNATIONAL" band, the fritted side bays with the dark strip above the canopy, and the central glazing head 2 m higher (tentative).

**Domestic (BD-01, BD-02, new BD-03; draw_domestic.py, new dom_bab_roof.py and dom_bab_roof.json)**
- **Pier roof edges, per pier:** BA-B +2.3 / −1.7 m, BA-D +2.4 / −1.4 m, BA-F 0.0 / −1.0 to −1.3 m (shapely, against the SFO Museum outlines). These replace the old summary in BX-01, the README and the BD-01 notes. The BA-F note in the spec was itself wrong and is corrected.
- **BA-B roof (BD-01):** now has, along the whole pier, the 3 planted roof wells, 2 bridges, 2 skylight grids and 3 PV fields. They were read by eye on NAIP (±3 m), shifted 5.1 m west for the roof lean, and clipped to the roof. The bridges continue west off the roof and may be walkway links.
- **BA-E (BD-02):** now stepped: raised centre roof, tapered edge overhanging the clerestory, lower side roofs. The step heights are inferred from photo a1.
- **New sheet BD-03:** landside elevations:
  - T1 Center, unrolled along its curved face (94.1 + 43.6 + 93.8 m): canopy, two-tier fritted wall, signage zone, PV at the roof edge. Heights are given above the departures curb from photo d1 and are low-confidence.
  - Terminal 2: the published description only; every dimension is marked unknown.

**Landside (BL-01, BL-02, BL-03; draw_landside.py)**
- **Tags:** the identities of the LTP 1 DOF points and the RCC "TANK" point are now inferred.
- **BL-02 Superbay:** the roof is dimensioned at 138 m along the spine against the 134.5 m outline, a difference of 1.75 m per end, labelled roof overhang or outline error.
- **BL-03 Superbay:** roofs now fall from the spine (41.15 m) to tips at about 27 m (22–32). That comes from photo l3, whose identification is unverified. A new door-face view shows the 8 folded bays and two door bays of about 67 m.
- **Grand Hyatt:** the task text was cut off. I took the fix to be drawing the face described in the spec, checked on the photo the spec cites. BL-03 now shows the dark podium under the south 47 %, the recessed colonnade level, the curtain wall with one spandrel per floor, the stepped penthouse and 4 corner masts. The spec's "taller block at the north end" is not visible in that photo; it is recorded as a conflict and not drawn.

**BX-01 (draw_compare.py)**
- **ITB roof row:** tags split: tips observed, DOF published, fit peak inferred, crown observed.
- **BA-A pod 1:** now reads "DOF 25.9 [pub] vs NAIP 22.3–25.2 [obs] (conflict)".
- **Superbay row:** now gives the tip height, and the dot plot uses DOF 40.23.

The four specs got correction or drawing notes (spec_tower.json, spec_domestic.json, spec_itb.json, spec_landside.json). Each buildings_*.md research note has a new "Drawing round 2" section. The README covers every change and adds BD-03 to the sheet list. The SVGs contain no embedded images; overlays stay in out/buildings/drawings.
open_questions: The Grand Hyatt finding was cut off in the task text after its first sentence. I took the fix to be drawing the face described in the spec (gh_plan_shape, gh_facade), checked on photo l4 (7391). Does the reviewer want anything more, for example a plan-shape change on BL-02?

Tower SW wing: the oblique photos fix only a tip at 254 deg, 14.0 m from the axis, which projects inside the flare from 297.7 deg. Only a photo from about 298 deg would settle whether the wing wraps south (silhouette up to u +13.6).

ITB: the canopy depth (drawn 5 m, inferred) controls which edge of the wall band holds; record drawings or a curb photo with a scale would settle it. The 64.0 m hall width against the 65.4 m roof is still an open conflict.
The departures-curb heights of T1 and T2 above the apron, and every T2 landside dimension, are unpublished; BD-03 marks them unknown.
Superbay: photo l3's identification is unverified, so the ~27 m tip height is low-confidence.
